header:
Date: 2025-12-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Luis Romero (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (BlueNova Eng Mgr), Priya Nair (BlueNova PM), Evan Song (BlueNova SRE), Tara Milton (BlueNova Security)
summary: POC weekly sync focused on defining SLO-gated rollout criteria, telemetry acceptance thresholds, and dry-run schedule. Discussed canary exit flags, rollback scenarios, and which dashboards/alerts must be green before shifting production traffic. Action items assigned for producing runbooks and telemetry exports.
topics: Latency vs cost tradeoffs and model variants
transcript:
00:00 Samir (AE): Alright everyone, good afternoon, thanks for joining. Quick check — audio good?
00:12 Jordan (Customer): Yep all good, can hear you.
00:18 Maya (SE): I'll share my screen in a sec, got the telemetry sheet open, also the runbook skeleton.
00:28 Priya (Customer PM): High level we're here to lock acceptance gates for the pilot cutover and make sure our SLOs are codified.
00:40 Samir: Exactly. We want a clear yes/no set of checks for the canary window and a short rollback path. Today we'll finalize thresholds and owners.
01:05 Evan (SRE): For context, our current prod p99 is around 640ms for the inference path, but with peak it's spiking toward 1.2s occasionally.
01:28 Luis (Redwood): Noted. On Redwood side we've got two candidate model variants: quantized 4-bit that saves cost but adds ~70ms p99, and FP16 which is faster but more expensive.
01:45 Jordan: And we need to be explicit about the cost tolerance; Priya has the budget constraints.
01:52 Priya: Correct, we can tolerate up to 20% unit cost increase during canary for acceptable latency gains, but sustained cost increases post-go-live need approval.
02:14 Maya: For SLO gating I propose these minimum checks during the canary 30 minute window: p99 <= 850ms, error rate <= 0.5%, tail latency regressions <= 10% versus baseline, and no uptick in 5xxs. If any fail, immediate rollback.
02:38 Tara (Security): Also want to confirm log retention and that KMS keys are rotated as per our policy. We'll need audit logs accessible for the canary window.
02:50 Samir: We'll include KMS audits in the list. Redwood's private deployment path supports your key manager; for hosted we can do envelope encryption with your KMS. I'll add a note.
03:15 Evan: For telemetry, we'll need Prom and our ingest logs for a 24-hour baseline, plus the canary 30-min dump. I can upload those.
03:32 Maya: Great, Evan, please include request/response size histograms and KV cache hit rates — those matter for token cost.
03:50 Jordan: What about A/B vs straight canary? We were thinking about A/B to test quality differences.
03:58 Luis: We can do an A/B split where 10% hits variant A (quantized) and 10% hits variant B (FP16), remainder to current. But that makes analysis slower. For cutover I'd recommend a progressive canary first.
04:20 Priya: Progressive canary sounds safer. We'll call out two gates: safety gate (errors/latency) and quality gate (manual sampling + auto rerank metrics).
04:38 Samir: For quality gate, Redwood can run prompt-level regression checks using your eval set and flag semantic regressions above X% — do we have the eval set?
04:48 Priya: We can provide a 500-prompt holdout. We'll feed that into the pilot harness.
05:05 Maya: Note there can be transcription mismatches in the model outputs; we'll add fuzzier similarity metrics not just exact-match.
05:25 Jordan: On escalation — if canary fails, what happens?
05:30 Samir: Immediate traffic rollback to previous model version and page the on-call SREs. We then run the incident runbook: collect trace ids, dump KV cache, gather mini-dump and open ticket. Luis will be on-call for the Redwood side.
05:49 Luis: Yup. I also want to call out a graceful degraded mode — if token generation latency spikes we can drop batching targets to favor latency at cost increase. That's in the runbook as an intermediate mitigation.
06:12 Priya: Does that require code changes?
06:15 Maya: No, it's runtime config: batch size and max queue age. We can adjust via the console and the change is immediate.
06:25 Tara: Security check — we need to verify SSO for the console and confirm RBAC roles for runbook operators.
06:33 Samir: We'll share the RBAC mappings and a screenshot of the SSO config.
06:50 Jordan: Can we get a readout of expected cost delta for FP16 vs quantized at our traffic levels?
06:58 Maya: I'll run a cost sweep with your qps profile. Expect roughly 30–40% savings with quantized but latencies up. I'll produce a table.
07:20 Evan: For the dry-run schedule — can we do non-business-hours rehearsal to reduce impact?
07:26 Priya: Yes let's aim for a weekend rehearsal, Dec 16 suggested earlier by Samir.
07:35 Samir: Proposed plan: 1) Dry-run (no real user traffic) Dec 16; 2) Rehearsal with 5–10% synthetic traffic Dec 18; 3) Go/no-go decision Dec 20.
07:50 Jordan: Sounds good.
08:03 Luis: Quick note on telemetry: Redwood will ship a Telemetry Acceptance Checklist, which includes exact metric names, query snippets (PromQL), and alert thresholds. That will be the single source of truth during the canary.
08:20 Samir: I'll attach the checklist to the runbook, link: https://redwood.internal/pilot-telemetry-checklist (shared doc).
08:30 Priya: We'll want a short checklist item that the data pipeline latency is under 60s for near-real-time dashboards.
08:36 Evan: That we can do. Our pipeline is typically <45s.
08:45 Maya: One more gating nuance — KV cache warmup: first 5 minutes will look worse until prefix cache stabilizes. We'll exclude first 10 minutes from the p99 gating window.
09:02 Jordan: Good call. Make sure that's documented so we don't prematurely roll back.
09:10 Samir: Documented.
09:18 Tara: Compliance question — do we have a SOC 2 type II report available for hosted? We may need it for procurement.
09:26 Samir: We do for hosted; private deployments get an attestation and we can provide the SOC report under NDA. I'll drop that in the security packet.
09:40 Priya: Anything else for runbook?
09:44 Maya: We'll add checkpoints: pre-cutover checklist, canary start, 10m, 30m, 60m checks, decision points, rollback steps, stakeholder pings.
10:05 Jordan: On metrics to watch: p99 latency, 5xx rate, token cost per request, KV cache hit rate, model quality drift (eval score).
10:18 Samir: For model quality drift, we'll set an automatic stop if semantic drift > 6% on the holdout set. Priya agreed?
10:27 Priya: Agree.
10:33 Evan: We'll provide dashboards access to Redwood in read-only row-level view for the pilot window.
10:40 Tara: Ensure logs redact PII before sharing.
10:45 Samir: We'll add a log-redaction step. Redwood supports field-level redaction during ingestion.
11:00 Luis: On fallback policies — we can route traffic by region if a zone is degraded, and fallback to cheaper model variants if latency SLOs are violated after several retries. That said, fallback should be last resort.
11:20 Jordan: Would prefer region routing before model fallback.
11:24 Luis: Agreed. We'll codify route priorities.
11:40 Priya: Let's capture acceptance sign-off process: Engineering (Jordan + Evan) greenlights telemetry, Product (Priya) greenlights quality, Security (Tara) greenlights compliance, Samir to coordinate Redwood sign-off.
11:58 Samir: I'll create a checklist with checkboxes and owners.
12:05 Maya: I'll also prepare an automated smoke-test harness that runs sample prompts against candidate variants and posts pass/fail into Slack channel.
12:16 Jordan: Please include failure rate thresholds for that harness.
12:22 Maya: Will do.
12:30 Priya: Ok, recap please?
12:34 Samir: Recap — Samir will send SLO gating checklist + runbook draft by Dec 11; Evan uploads baseline telemetry by Dec 12; Maya runs latency/cost sweep by Dec 15; dry-run on Dec 16; rehearsal Dec 18; go/no-go Dec 20. Action items logged.
12:54 Jordan: Thanks everyone.
13:00 Samir: Thank you, we'll follow up in email with links. Meeting adjourned.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts — "KV" sometimes transcribed as "K V" and product names may be slightly off in auto notes. Shared artifacts: https://redwood.internal/pilot-telemetry-checklist , https://blue-nova.s3/pilot-telemetry-baseline (placeholder).
footnotes: Transcript contains natural disfluencies, some speaker attributions may be approximate. See action items and next steps for concrete follow-ups.
